title: Hunting, fishing and trapping kit
summary: Gear for taking food from the land and turning it into safe meat: what to carry when you hunt, fish, trap and dress game, and what to have at home to cut up and keep it. From NYS DEC hunter, trapper and fishing education material and extension game-care guides.

items.text: A sharp knife for field dressing
items.note: Use it for game only, not your kitchen knives. Clean it often as you work.

items.text: A whetstone or steel for sharpening
A small hatchet or saw
items.note: Cut joints with a knife where you can, and avoid sawing into bone: see Butchering deer and small game. Never cut meat with a blade you used on bone.

items.text: Disposable rubber, nitrile or latex gloves
items.note: Always; above all with rabbits, hares and rodents, and if your hands have cuts or sores.

items.text: Clean cloths or paper towels, and sanitizing wipes
Several feet of rope or nylon cord, and a drag rope
Rubber bands, string or twist ties
items.note: For tying off the vent and bladder.

items.text: Sealable plastic bags
items.note: For the guts to go in the trash, and for the heart and liver when Butchering deer and small game says to keep them.

items.text: Game bags, cheesecloth or clean cotton bags (a clean pillow case will do)
items.note: To keep flies and dirt off meat while it cools.

items.text: A large cooler with ice or snow
items.note: Bags of ice or snow, or jugs of ice, also go inside a deer to cool it.

items.text: Clean drinking water
A full-body safety harness with a lifeline and foot strap, and a haul line, if you hunt from a tree stand
Hunter orange clothing
items.note: New York’s rule for deer and bear is in New York rules for hunting, fishing and trapping.

items.text: Knife, phone, flashlight and whistle carried in your pockets
Headlamp or flashlight, with spare batteries
Map, compass or GPS
Binoculars
items.note: To identify your target and what is behind it. Never use a rifle scope as binoculars.

items.text: Fluorescent orange flagging tape
Water and high-energy food for the day
First aid kit
Warm layers that wick sweat (no cotton), a wind- and water-resistant outer layer, and extra gloves
A deer cart, if you have one
items.note: Saves your back on the drag.

items.text: Rod and reel: a spin-casting outfit for beginners
Monofilament fishing line
items.note: Eight-pound test is a good all-round weight.

items.text: Hooks, sinkers, bobbers, swivels and snap-swivels
items.note: Size 6 to 8 Aberdeen hooks for panfish.

items.text: Bait or lures
Needle-nose pliers for hooks, line clippers, a net, a bucket and a towel
A ruler, to check fish against the legal size in normal times
Ice safety picks, for ice fishing or trapping on ice
Ice gear: a spud bar or hand auger, a jigging rod or hand line, tip-ups, boots with cleats, and a sled for hauling
A life jacket for each person in a boat, and an inflatable one for trapping in water
A pack basket, bucket or sack to carry trapping gear
Traps that are legal in normal times, and extra trap tags
items.note: Which traps are legal, and how each must be marked, are in New York rules for hunting, fishing and trapping.

items.text: Gloves for setting traps, long rubber gloves for water sets, and a heavy pair for handling animals
Setting tongs, a safety gripper and a rope with a loop in one end, whenever you use large body-gripping traps
items.note: How to use the rope to free yourself is in Trapping.

items.text: Trap stakes, wire or cable, pliers and cable cutters
A trowel or other digging tool, a dirt sifter and a kneeling pad
Hip boots or chest waders, for water sets
A catchpole
items.note: To control a trapped animal so it can be released or dispatched more safely.

items.text: Waterproof matches and fire starters
At home: a boning or fillet knife, a meat saw, a gambrel or stout stick, and a table to work on
Airtight bags or wrap, and a marker to label and date meat
Plain, unscented household bleach
items.note: For the knife and tool soak in Butchering deer and small game, and the mixes in Clean and disinfect.

items.text: A food thermometer, and a thermometer for the cooler or the place meat hangs
Food-grade salt with no additives such as iodine
items.note: For brining. Ways to keep meat, and their risks, are in Preserving game meat.
